value.body: A UI/UX designer decides how a digital product works and looks — from the steps a user takes to the layout of each screen. Software companies, start-ups, digital agencies and in-house tech teams hire them. A typical day includes reviewing research, sketching flows, building prototypes and working closely with developers and product managers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Des (interaction, communication or UX), or any degree with a strong portfolio

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Figma or similar design tools, prototyping and whiteboarding tools

items.label: B.Des students enrolled
items.note: All design specialisations and years; about 72% are women

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Hiring is largely portfolio-based: freshers show 2–4 case studies explaining the problem, process and result. B.Des graduates often enter through campus placement or a final-year internship that converts to a job.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior designer, product designer, design lead.
Entry-level competition is high, and portfolio quality matters more than the degree name.
Basic understanding of front-end code helps in working with developers.

competition.note: B.Des graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
